item.title: Ohio senator says former son-in-law shouldn't be in Congress amid abuse claims
item.description: GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio says his former son-in-law Rep. Max Miller isn't fit to serve in the House after he was accused of abusing Moreno's daughter and granddaughter. Miller, also an Ohio Republican, disputed the allegations and says he has no plans to leave office. Nikole Killion has the latest.

item.title: Spokane residents lose homes, struggle with wildfire destruction: "All of our memories are gone"
item.description: A fast-moving wildfire ripped through Spokane, Washington, and destroyed hundreds of structures over the weekend. Residents are working to recover after losing all of their belongings. CBS News' Kris Van Cleave has more.

item.title: Iran denies Trump claim that U.S-Iran negotiations begin today
item.description: Tehran said Monday it had no plans to hold direct talks with the U.S., despite President Trump's claim that a "deal is imminent."

item.title: Off-duty state trooper and civilian credited with helping stop Idaho In-N-Out shooter
item.description: Officials say three people were killed and seven were injured in a shooting at an In-N-Out in Idaho over the weekend. Officials believe the shooter acted alone and are investigating possible motives. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Todd Blanche rescinds controversial "anti-weaponization fund" that turned off 2 Republicans
item.description: Todd Blanche, whose Senate confirmation for attorney general is set for Tuesday, officially rescinded the "anti-weaponization fund" late Sunday night that two Republican senators protested. CBS News' Weijia Jiang has the latest.

item.title: Sleep problems could be linked to work-related stress, study finds
item.description: Researchers tracking the sleep of men and women in the U.K. between the ages of 50 and 66 found nearly 70% experienced persistent sleep problems, and many may be linked closely to work-related stress. Sleep psychologist Shelby Harris explains how it could impact your health and how to create better sleep habits.

item.title: Trump says new talks expected to start with Iran, but Tehran disputes claim
item.description: President Trump says talks are expected to begin again with Iran on Monday and initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. But Tehran says there are no planned direct talks with the White House, only discussions with Oman. Imtiaz Tyab has more.

item.title: Death toll mounts after migrants rush into Spain from Morocco, find little help
item.description: Some of the nearly 60,000 migrants who rushed the border of Ceuta on Thursday still remain in the Spanish territory, but many have returned to Morocco voluntarily, officials said. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has the latest.

item.title: How to negotiate a lower home price in today's economy, according to experts
item.description: You may not have to pay asking price for the home you're eyeing right now, experts say. Here's how to do that.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom note said she died, sheriff says investigation is still active and mounting
item.description: The investigation into Nancy Guthrie's disappearance is still "very active," Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos said after two ransom notes were released. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Eye Opener: Wildfires in western U.S. force evacuations, destroy homes
item.description: Fast-moving wildfires in the West consume hundreds of structures and force thousands from their homes. Plus, Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinds President Trump's "anti-weaponization fund" as his nomination is on the line. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Trump says U.S.-Iran talks will resume today after threatening attacks not seen since World War II
item.description: President Trump says he called off a massive attack on Iran and said that negotiations would start Monday, which Iran is denying. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has the latest.

item.title: Can Blanche win back Republican Senate support after rescinding "anti-weaponization" fund?
item.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche is on track for his Senate confirmation after formally rescinding the "anti-weaponization fund" that led to grievances among some Republicans. CBS News' Taurean Small has more.

item.title: Zac Brown Band surprises 37,000 Fenway Park concert fans with free cruises
item.description: Zac Brown Band celebrated their 15th straight sold-out concert at Fenway Park in Boston by giving everyone a free vacation on a cruise ship.

item.title: Ariana Grande pulls out of musical over "endless, ongoing public scrutiny"
item.description: Ariana Grande had been due to star alongside her "Wicked" co-star Jonathan Bailey in a production of "Sunday in the Park with George" in 2027.

item.title: Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting suspect identified after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: Fast-moving wildfires in Spokane area destroy hundreds of homes
item.description: Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown called the wildfires burning through the area the "worst natural disaster our region has faced."

item.title: Suspect arrested in Greece after U.K. woman's body found in suitcase
item.description: Police say the suspect transported the body to an abandoned site in a suitcase and subsequently used her bank cards to withdraw money.

item.title: RFK Jr., Oz blame ACA enrollment drop on fraud, but experts cite rising costs
item.description: Rising premiums forced many people in Affordable Care Act plans to give up their coverage. But the Trump administration claims a huge drop in enrollment is almost entirely due to its fraud crackdown.

item.title: U.S.-Iran negotiations set to begin Monday, Trump says after calling off strikes
item.description: President Trump said negotiations with Iran are set to begin Monday after announcing Saturday night that he canceled a pending attack on Iran.

item.title: Acting attorney general issues order rescinding "anti-weaponization fund"
item.description: The order came after Republican Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn threatened to block Blanche's confirmation for Attorney General if the fund was not rescinded in writing.

item.title: Trump says outline of Iran deal agreed to, mediators say otherwise, strikes on hold for now
item.description: President Trump has called off new attacks on Iran for the time being, insisting an end to the war is close. He's also again calling for the "immediate" re-opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: New details on deadly In-N-Out shooting
item.description: New details are emerging about this weekend's deadly mass shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho. At least three people were killed in the attack and seven others wounded. Lindsey Reiser reports.

item.title: Mass evacuations underway as wildfires bear down on Spokane, Washington
item.description: Explosive wildfires in Spokane, Washington, have destroyed more than 600 structures, many of them within the city limits. The fast-moving flames led to mass evacuations and chaos, as families fled their homes. Adam Yamaguchi reports and Andrew Kozak looks at the forecast and the record heat threatening 50 million Americans.

item.title: 8/2/2026: Lourdes; The Improbable Tale of Ted Lasso; Birds of War
item.description: First, investigating medically unexplained cures. Then, a look behind the scenes of "Ted Lasso." And, birders flock here since guerrillas disarmed.

item.title: 8/2: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Mass evacuations underway as wildfires bear down on Spokane, Washington; New details on deadly In-N-Out shooting.

item.title: Hugging Face CEO calls hack by rogue OpenAI model "very weird and unprecedented"
item.description: An artificial intelligence model that was being tested by OpenAI went rogue and hacked the firm Hugging Face on its own, in what Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue called a "very weird and unprecedented" incident.

item.title: 8/2: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly and Republican Rep. Mike Turner discuss Iran. Plus, the CEO of Hugging Face discusses an alarming incident in which OpenAI's technology went rogue and hacked into his company. And former Sen. Joe Manchin discusses his push to elect more independents.

item.title: Spain's Ceuta grapples with aftermath of border surge
item.description: Dozens died, and the tiny enclave of Ceuta was thrown into chaos earlier this week after a rush of migrants entered from Morocco.

item.title: Flights canceled as WestJet flight attendants strike over pay dispute
item.description: WestJet canceled more than 300 flights as of early Sunday, snarling travel plans in Canada in the middle of a three-day weekend.
